solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Underwater swimmer drives excitedly across Caribbean island

indicators.note: the scrambled drives stretches across, so it is split around the island's name
doing something excitedly suggests jumbling, so the letters of drives are rearranged

parts.note: Cuba is the largest Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A diver motors eagerly over a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver using breathing apparatus swims underwater, so the phrase describes one.

clue.text: Crowd going to the Spanish lodging house

parts.note: a host is a large crowd, as in a host of people
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A crowd heads to a Spanish guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostel is a cheap establishment offering beds to travellers, a kind of lodging house.

clue.text: Judge first half of recipe book

indicators.note: the opening three letters of the six-letter word recipe are taken

parts.note: to book a meal or seat is to order it

explanation.surface: Someone is weighing up the opening section of a cookbook.
explanation.walkthrough: In England and Wales a recorder is a barrister or solicitor sitting as a part-time judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorder is a part-time judge in the English courts, a specialised legal title.

clue.text: Rum does when served up — and port

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so the letters of does are rearranged
in a down clue served up means read upwards, so the word turns backwards

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as he arrived

explanation.surface: Drinks are served: rum, and port to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' and 'port' both look like drinks; rum is the anagram signal and port the definition. 'served up' turns AS into SA after ODES.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port city in Ukraine.

clue.text: Awful long wait for sleeping car

indicators.note: something awful is in a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A traveller endures a dreadful delay for a berth on the train.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon-lit is the French term for a railway carriage fitted with berths.

clue.text: First to recognise a French character from the past

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: une is the feminine French for a

explanation.surface: The first to recognise a historical French figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A rune is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet, so a written character from long ago.

clue.text: Hurricane series being shown inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a cycle is a series of works or events
a film being shown is on

explanation.surface: A television series about a hurricane is being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a violent rotating storm, the same weather system as a hurricane.

clue.text: Church member allowed to keep pair, and article worn on the wrist

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
a brace is a pair, as in a brace of pheasants
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A churchgoer may keep a couple of pieces of jewellery on.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm bracelet is a chain worn round the wrist hung with small trinkets.

clue.text: Copper strangled by a fat round count

indicators.note: being strangled means being gripped round the neck, so one piece is held inside another
round signals turning about, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: lard is pig fat
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman is throttled by a portly villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the element. A LARD turned round gives DRALA, which closes around CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Dracula is the vampire nobleman of Bram Stoker's novel, a Transylvanian count.

clue.text: What stealing a fluid is?

parts.note: taking anything that is not yours, liquid or otherwise, breaks the rules of the land

explanation.surface: A question about the legal status of pinching some liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft of any kind is a crime, so it is contrary to legislation.

clue.text: Bird in brass — a lot manufactured

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up, so these letters are made into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird figure is made in brass, lots of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The albatross is a large seabird with a vast wingspan.

clue.text: Love game analysed, last of a series

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: to analyse is to break down, so the letters of game are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A love match is picked apart in the final of a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the end of any sequence.

clue.text: Gong bringing first of diners into dinner, perhaps

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: dinner is one example of a meal, hence perhaps

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the word diners

explanation.surface: A gong is struck to bring the diners in to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The gong looks like the dinner gong; it is slang for a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for an award or decoration, a medal.

clue.text: Pride, say, shown by unerring opener for Surrey, batting

parts.note: deadly accuracy is unerring aim

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, with a cricket batting pun

parts.note: a cricket batsman who is batting is in

explanation.surface: A Surrey opening batsman's flawless innings shows pride.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county with a famous cricket club; in cricket the side batting is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride is one of the seven cardinal sins of Christian teaching, hence an example.

clue.text: Gymnastic feat in heyday heard by experienced sailor on radio

indicators.note: something on radio is only heard, so the words are judged by sound

parts.note: a heyday is one's summer, and an experienced sailor is an old salt; heard by joins summer to salt

explanation.surface: A retired seaman recalls on the radio a tumbling trick from his youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard by' joins SUMMER (heyday) to SALT (experienced sailor); 'on radio' says the pair is judged by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A somersault is a full head-over-heels rotation, a classic tumbling move.

clue.text: Two ways of viewing something that invigorates?

indicators.note: the word reads the same viewed from either end, forwards or backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something refreshing can be seen two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviver is a tonic or pick-me-up that restores energy.

clue.text: Purchase not fashionable, a robe

indicators.note: not says one piece is taken away from the other

parts.note: buying shares or property is an investment
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: Buying an unfashionable robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a ceremonial garment, especially one worn by clergy, so a robe.

clue.text: Try to attract volunteers over first

indicators.note: first says the turned volunteers come at the front, before the other piece
over signals turning the abbreviation for the volunteers back to front

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
to tempt is to attract or lure

explanation.surface: An effort to lure volunteers before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns TA into AT, and 'first' puts it ahead of TEMPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Try and attempt are synonyms as nouns, meaning an effort.

clue.text: Review a penny parking increase

parts.note: P is the road-sign letter for parking
a raise is an increase, especially in pay

explanation.surface: Reviewing a rise of a penny on parking charges.
explanation.definitionFit: To review and to appraise both mean to assess or evaluate something.

clue.text: Character cutting could be a cheat

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing character
a cutting remark is sharp

explanation.surface: An eccentric with a cutting edge might be cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' also suggests cutting the deck, which suits the card cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A card-sharp is someone who cheats at cards for gain.

clue.text: Going up a track

parts.note: a scent is the trail a hound follows

explanation.surface: Climbing a trail.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb, the act of rising or going upward.

clue.text: Spoil church procession

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

explanation.surface: Ruining a church parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is an organised walk in formation, such as a procession or demonstration.

clue.text: Guide worked with hands

definitions.meaning: operated by hand rather than by machine

explanation.definitionFit: A manual is a book of instructions, and manual work is done by hand.

clue.text: Relief comes as swelling reduced round middle section of hock

indicators.note: round means placed around, so one piece encloses the other
reduced means cut short, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a lump is a swelling

indicators.note: the inner letters of the word hock are taken, losing its ends

explanation.surface: Relief arrives when a swollen leg joint goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts LUMP to LUM, which goes round OC from hOCk. 'Relief' looks medical but means a stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or priest standing in temporarily, giving relief to the usual one.

clue.text: Form of fuel used in Morocco — kerosene

indicators.note: used in means contained within, so the letters are found inside the words

explanation.surface: A type of fuel burnt in Morocco is kerosene.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is a solid fuel made by heating coal without air.

clue.text: Correspondence after series identifying armour

indicators.note: after says the letters come after the other piece

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked events or things
mail is letters and correspondence

explanation.surface: After a run of letters someone is recognised as wearing armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain mail is armour made of interlocking metal rings.

clue.text: Seen and understood

definitions.meaning: observed, as when sights are absorbed by a visitor
grasped, as when information is absorbed

explanation.definitionFit: Taking in a view means seeing it, and taking in facts means grasping them.

clue.text: Onset of whooping in sickly bird

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sallow means of a sickly yellowish complexion

indicators.note: the onset is the beginning, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A bird with a whooping cough looks sickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Onset of whooping' suggests whooping cough; it just gives W.
explanation.definitionFit: The swallow is a migratory songbird with a forked tail.
